I hit the tool limit mid-investigation, so here's where things stand. No archive yet — but the diagnosis is complete and certain, and I want to hand you the fix rather than a guess.

First, a note on inputs
No dump.txt was attached this session. Rather than ask and lose the turn, I pulled the tree straight from GitHub at commit a2731102a1 (2026-08-18 09:37Z, "add claude changes") — which is exactly the post-Slice-48 state, so the reconstruction is byte-exact rather than hash-verified-approximate. That worked well enough that it may be worth preferring over dump.txt in future, though it only sees what you've pushed.

The failure: the implementation is right, the test's arithmetic is wrong
ResequencingOneHeadingLeavesTheOtherHeadingAlone arranges Tea@0, Coffee@1, Cola@2 via ThreeItemsAsync, then resequences to [cola, tea, coffee].

That is a rotation, not a swap. Cola 2→0, Tea 0→1, Coffee 1→2 — all three move, so three reordered events is correct behaviour under the rule the verb documents ("one event per item whose position actually changed"). Actual 3 is right; expected 2 is the defect.

The provenance is visible: OnlyTheItemsThatMovedGetAnEvent, forty lines up, uses [cola, coffee, tea] — a reversal, which leaves Coffee at 1 and writes exactly two rows. The new fact took that count and paired it with the rotation from ResequencingAssignsPositionsFromThePlaceInTheList. The comment // Two events, both under Drinks carried the wrong half across. Nothing about the verb, the WHERE clause, or the UUIDv7 fix is implicated — and the sibling assertions (Assert.Empty on trifle and sorbet, [0, 1] on their positions) prove the isolation claim the fact actually exists for, which is why they passed.

The repair I intend: keep the rotation, correct the count to 3, and record in the fact's own summary why 3 rather than 2 — because with a rotation the total equals the number of items listed, so this fact no longer witnesses the per-row no-op rule and OnlyTheItemsThatMovedGetAnEvent is the fact that does. Keeping the rotation is deliberate: it writes every row under the touched heading, which is the stronger probe for a WHERE clause that reaches one row too far. Reversing to [cola, coffee, tea] and leaving the 2 is the alternative, and it is the one to prefer if you'd rather this fact keep both properties — say so and I'll flip it. Either way the fact count stays 8, so 1190 → 1191 with the one new fact below.

The menu progress I'd pair with it
The last outstanding piece of Stage 3's guest-menu paragraph: a section's own description under its heading. The plan named two routes ("a second read or a widened record") and deferred rather than guessing. I'd widen — MenuItemSummary gains MenuSectionDescription as one more aliased column on the INNER JOIN that already carries MenuSectionName, and the guest surface renders it under the <h4>.

The argument for widening over a second read is a tearing one, not a performance one: two reads at two instants let a heading render its new name beside its old description, and one row of one query cannot do that. There is only one construction site to follow (OrderStagingTests.Item), so the cost is genuinely small.

This is a ruling reversal you may want to veto. MenuSectionOnTheMenu's summary currently says a surface needing the description "would read the directory rather than widen this," and three other prose sites say guests don't read it yet — MenuWorkflow.DescribeMenuSectionAsync, MenuWiringTests, and the section editor's own lede. All four go stale the moment this renders, which is precisely why they were worded to anticipate it.

The cheap win I didn't expect: scenario 17 already creates "Starters" with the description "Something to begin with." and "Puddings" with none. So the end-to-end assertion is two lines plus a harness reader — the sentence arriving and its absence, both through a browser.

Files this touches: MenuDirectory.cs, TableOrderSurface.razor, app.css, OrderStagingTests.cs, MenuWorkflow.cs, MenuWiringTests.cs, ManageMenuSection.razor, MenuDirectoryTests.cs (+1 fact, so §16.4's MenuDirectoryTests count moves 7 → 8), TableOrderJourneys.cs, EndToEndScenarios.cs, plus the five documents and _CHANGES.md. Spec goes v1.33 → v1.34, F-99 gets a ledger row, nothing to delete, and git add will be needed for no new files under this plan.

Say continue and I'll author and package it. If you'd rather I ship the one-line test fix alone first for a clean green run before the widening lands, say that instead — it's the sequencing discipline this project usually applies, and I'd not argue against it.
